CareerEconomy.funds.reason: Funds really do integrate under a career overhaul, and none of these four is the derivative on its own. The balance moves at subsidy MINUS upkeep, so a reckoning wants a composed expression rather than a field pairing; the min and max are the envelope the subsidy sits in and are not rates in effect at all; and the impulses that actually dominate the balance (a contract award, a launch, a facility upgrade) are described by none of them. Also conditional on the elected model: stock answers all four as zero, so a reckoning fitted to them would hold the balance still through every purchase.

CareerEconomy.reputation.reason: A true derivative and the sign is the trap: reputation FALLS by this, so integrating it forward adds where it should subtract. It is also state-dependent rather than constant, being a fixed portion of the current reputation applied daily, which makes the honest model an exponential decay and not a linear ramp. Zero on stock, which has no decay at all.

CareerEconomy.unlockCredit.reason: The allowance genuinely does accrue continuously, and its rate is not on the wire and is not any of these four. RP-1 grows it as a fraction of the researcher salary bill, a band that falls from 0.6 to 0.1 as the research department grows, and ONLY while a tech node is actually progressing in the research queue: an idle queue accrues nothing however large the payroll. So the nearest true rate is a slice of upkeep.researchSalary gated on a condition no field expresses, and upkeepPerDay is the whole outgoing bill rather than that slice. Spending is impulsive too, drawn at a part, upgrade or tooling purchase and at nothing else. Absent entirely under stock, so a reckoning fitted here would be describing one install's mod.

CareerStrategy.dateActivated.reason: Dimensional degeneracy, not a pairing: `divide({s:1},{s:1})` is `{}` and `1`/`ratio`/`%` are all dimensionless, so EVERY dimensionless field is the dimensional rate of EVERY time field in its own type. `ecc` is not the rate of an epoch. This is what the algebra says and no vocabulary work fixes it; it is the single strongest argument against deriving a class from units.

CrashFlightStats.groundDistance.reason: An immutable accident report. Every field is a recorded peak or total from a flight that has ended, so there is nothing left to integrate, and a peak speed is not the rate of a peak altitude in any case.

CrewRosterEntry.retiresAtUt.reason: Dimensional degeneracy, the same case as the standing's own end date beside it, with one difference worth stating: this one is not integrated from anything at all. A career overhaul reads a retirement date out of its own settings when the kerbal is hired and pushes it back in discrete steps as they fly, so there is no rate to find, let alone one of these. Courage and stupidity in particular are personality stats that never change.

CrewRosterEntry.standingEndsAtUt.reason: Dimensional degeneracy, and worth writing down rather than waving away because of what it lands next to. `divide({s:1},{s:1})` is `{}`, so every dimensionless field on the roster is offered as the derivative of every date on it, and a kerbal's courage is not the rate at which their training finishes. What makes it more than noise is that one of the standings behind this date genuinely IS integrable and this rule still cannot reach it: a training course's ETA is remaining build points over a build rate, both in a career overhaul's own `bp`/`bp/s` vocabulary, which core cannot dimension. The producer already derives the date from them, so there is nothing left for a client to integrate.

KerbalismCrewRule.value.reason: Claimed, and NOT by integrating the sibling the rule offered. `degenPerSec` is a config constant off `Profile.rules[].degeneration` that applies only once the rule's input resource is gone, so integrating it would advance a supplied kerbal towards their fatal threshold on schedule.
